> I want to design a portable modular computer with interchangeable modules attached underneath using side screws. The modules will connect to the main unit through power and data connectors. My first prototype will focus on the enclosure, the mounting system, and one working expansion module. Future modules could include extra USB ports, a battery pack, and a drone storage and charging dock, with software on the computer to communicate with a compatible drone.

## Design

### 2026-10-01 — I developed the concept for ModuDeck using my hand-drawn sketches. I defined a portable computer with full-size stackable modules for a drone, batteries, and storage drives. I also planned a flip-up t

**3h**

I developed the concept for ModuDeck using my hand-drawn sketches. I defined a portable computer with full-size stackable modules for a drone, batteries, and storage drives. I also planned a flip-up touchpad revealing a small phone, with a dialing keypad on its right, plus rear connections for antennas, power, and data. With AI assistance, I generated concept blueprints and preliminary 3D models to visualize the idea. Dimensions, electronic components, wiring, and connector specifications still need to be selected and validated.

### 2026-10-02 — I refined the ModuDeck concept, focusing on the computer and three empty stackable expansion trays. The layout keeps a fixed keyboard, a flip-up touchpad revealing a small phone, and a dialing keypad

**3h**

I refined the ModuDeck concept, focusing on the computer and three empty stackable expansion trays. The layout keeps a fixed keyboard, a flip-up touchpad revealing a small phone, and a dialing keypad on its right.

With AI assistance(my ai), I explored new improvements: alignment guides, side screws with threaded inserts, removable rear port panels, cable strain relief, ventilation openings, protective corners, rubber feet, and a folding carry handle.

The three attached images are AI-generated concept illustrations, not photographs of a built prototype or validated CAD renders. The proposed improvements still need to be incorporated into the CAD and checked against actual component dimensions. Electrical connections, power requirements, printing tolerances, and mechanical strength remain to be verified.

### 2026-10-02 — With my AI assistance made by me

**5h**

With my AI assistance made by me

, I documented the initial electrical design for ModuDeck after removing the phone and dialing keypad. The project now focuses on the computer, a fixed touchpad, and three empty stackable trays.

I prepared five wiring drawings covering the overall system, USB connections, display cables, an optional Pico LED circuit, and a pushbutton circuit. The LED uses a 1 kΩ resistor, while the button uses a 10 kΩ pull-up resistor.

These are preliminary drawings, not tested hardware. The next steps are to select the exact display and USB hub, verify their power requirements, and test the circuits before integrating them into the enclosure.![circiito6](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/dnf0QiY8U5i5iBpbsyYlTiK3wkfqnu8r/dfd8ea7724491564434c6bba5bb04216ca99900261044e36247b18b5bf284e5a.png)
